chief_complaint: sudden generalized swelling with heavy proteinuria
hpi_details: A 32-year-old female presents with sudden onset of generalized swelling (face, legs, abdomen) that developed over just a few days, along with foamy urine and unintentional weight gain. She denies recent infection, new medications, or NSAID use, and otherwise feels well aside from mild fatigue.
ideas: She thinks her sudden puffiness and weight gain might be a severe allergic reaction to something she ate or an acute thyroid issue.
concerns: She is worried her heart is failing and that she will collapse while looking after her toddler alone at home.
expectations: She hopes to receive a fast-acting water pill today to drain the fluid and make her shoes and clothes fit again.

clinical_knowledge.topic: Minimal Change Disease evaluation and management
core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Minimal Change Disease is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Standard management for adult minimal change disease involves nephrology referral and generally a kidney biopsy to confirm the diagnosis before starting therapy (unlike in children, where empiric steroids are standard), followed by oral corticosteroids and monitoring of urine protein, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: sudden generalized swelling in child with heavy proteinuria

Key HPI features: A 32-year-old female presents with sudden onset of generalized swelling (face, legs, abdomen) that developed over just a few days, along with foamy urine and unintentional weight gain. She denies recent infection, new medications, or NSAID use, and otherwise feels well aside from mild fatigue.

Objective/Exam findings: Vitals: BP 118/76, HR 88, afebrile, weight up 4kg from baseline. 3+ pitting edema of face, legs, and abdomen (ascites). Labs: serum albumin 1.9 g/dL, 24-hour urine protein 6.5g, urinalysis with no hematuria, normal complement levels, normal renal function.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Minimal Change Disease.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to FSGS without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Fever or abdominal pain — increased infection risk with nephrotic syndrome.
management_principles: Involve nephrology and obtain a kidney biopsy to confirm the diagnosis before starting corticosteroids in this adult patient
Start oral Prednisone once biopsy-confirmed, and monitor daily urine protein
Counsel patient on infection risk, edema management, and thrombosis precautions
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guideline for Kidney Disease

reference_soap.subjective: 32F presents with sudden onset of generalized swelling (face, legs, abdomen) that developed over just a few days, along with foamy urine and unintentional weight gain. Denies recent infection, new medications, or NSAID use.
reference_soap.objective: Vitals: BP 118/76, HR 88, afebrile, weight up 4kg from baseline. 3+ pitting edema of face, legs, and abdomen (ascites). Labs: serum albumin 1.9 g/dL, 24-hour urine protein 6.5g, urinalysis with no hematuria, normal complement levels, normal renal function.
reference_soap.assessment: Nephrotic syndrome with heavy proteinuria, hypoalbuminemia, and normal complement/renal function, most consistent with minimal change disease — though in an adult, biopsy confirmation is needed before treatment, unlike the empiric steroid approach used in children.
reference_soap.plan: Confirm nephrotic syndrome and evaluate secondary causes with serum albumin, kidney function, urine protein quantification, and appropriate serologies. In an adult with suspected minimal change disease, involve Nephrology and generally obtain a kidney biopsy before initiating glucocorticoids unless a clear alternative pathway applies. Monitor edema, kidney function, thrombotic risk, and response to treatment.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Minimal Change Disease
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Minimal Change Disease
Implement evidence-based management plan: Oral Prednisone, monitor daily urine protein

teaching.one_liner: The most common cause of nephrotic syndrome in children, with sudden generalized swelling and heavy proteinuria from podocyte injury not visible on light microscopy — usually very steroid-responsive.
red_flags: Fever or abdominal pain — increased infection risk with nephrotic syndrome

must_ask.say: How quickly did the swelling appear?

history.answer: My whole body swelled up out of nowhere over the last few days, and my clothes and shoes suddenly feel way too tight.
It started around my eyes and face, but within three or four days my belly and both of my legs puffed up as well.
It happened very fast, just over three or four days, and it seems to get worse each day.
My eyes and face look puffiest when I wake up in the morning, and my legs and feet feel heavier by nighttime.
Yes, when I press my shins, deep dents stay there for a long time, and my socks leave deep grooves.
I weighed myself yesterday and I am up about 4 kilograms from my usual weight, even though I have not eaten more.
Yes, I noticed lots of white bubbles and foam in the toilet when I pee, and they do not flush away easily.
The color looks pale yellow, not red or cola-colored, but I feel like I am peeing slightly less volume than usual.
No, I have not had any fever, chills, or stomach pain at all.
No, I can breathe fine, and I do not get winded when lying flat on my back or waking up at night.
No, both legs look the same and neither calf feels warm, red, or sore.
Yes, my stomach feels tight and bloated, like it is filled with fluid, but it does not hurt.
No, my eyes and skin are not yellow, and I have not had nosebleeds, bleeding gums, or easy bruising.
No, I have not had a sore throat, skin boils, or any colds recently.
No, I did not get any bee stings, start any new foods or laundry detergents, or take any painkillers like ibuprofen.
I feel a little tired, but I do not feel unusually sensitive to the cold, my skin is not dry, and my bowels are normal.
My appetite is about the same, and I have had no nausea, chronic diarrhea, or poor nutrition.
I do not eat particularly salty food, and my job does not require standing on my feet all day.
No, I have not had any surgery, long airplane flights, bed rest, or cancer.
I thought maybe I was having an extreme allergic reaction to some new food, or that my thyroid just completely shut down overnight.
I'm really scared my heart is giving out and that I might collapse while taking care of my toddler alone at home.
I'm hoping you can give me some kind of water pill today to quickly get rid of all this fluid so I can fit into my clothes again.
I have always been healthy and have never had high blood pressure, diabetes, kidney issues, or heart trouble.
I have never had any surgeries and I have never been admitted to a hospital.
I am not taking any prescription medications, birth control pills, herbal remedies, or over-the-counter pain relievers.
I have no known allergies to any medications, foods, or materials.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used e-cigarettes.
I only have a glass of wine or beer socially once or twice a month, and I have never had hepatitis.
I work in an office at a desk and live in an apartment with my husband.
Nobody in my family has had kidney disease, autoimmune disorders, dialysis, or early heart problems.
My last period was two weeks ago on schedule, my cycles are regular, and there is no chance I am pregnant.

exam.finding: Blood pressure is 118/76 mmHg, pulse 88 bpm, respiratory rate 16 breaths/min, oxygen saturation 99% on room air, temperature 36.7 C, with a 4 kg weight gain.
Mildly fatigued female with visible periorbital swelling and facial puffiness, in no acute respiratory distress.
Conjunctivae are pink and sclerae are anicteric without pallor or jaundice.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, smooth, non-tender, and moves freely with deglutition without nodules.
Jugular venous pressure is within normal limits at approximately 2 cm above the sternal angle; no distended neck veins.
Normal S1 and S2 heart sounds with regular rhythm; no third heart sound (S3), friction rub, or murmurs heard.
Lungs are clear to auscultation bilaterally with equal vesicular breath sounds and no crackles, wheezes, or rhonchi.
Symmetrically distended abdomen without prominent superficial veins, spider angiomas, or caput medusae.
Abdomen is soft and non-tender to light and deep palpation, with no guarding, rigidity, hepatomegaly, or splenomegaly.
Demonstrates shifting dullness and a perceptible fluid wave consistent with ascites.
Symmetric 3+ pitting edema extending up both pretibial surfaces to mid-shin, leaving persistent indentations on release.
Both calves are symmetric in circumference without localized warmth, erythema, cord-like induration, or calf tenderness.
